overall_reason: The system UI stack (Segoe UI drew every glyph at 1440 per fonts.json; system-ui computed at 375) sets every role, which fits a product-UI (Operate) composition on a 13/12px ladder, but the 26-character role 'Editor with comment access' breaks onto two right-aligned lines, and the invited email is cut to 'alexandra.whitfield@northwind...'.

score.reason: T-HEADLINE-FIT: the long name wraps cleanly over two lines, but the role label wraps mid-phrase and the email truncates. The type does not absorb either long-content case.

findings.title: Lines break where the sense breaks
findings.evidence: In dom-1440.json 'Editor with comment access' is 12px in a 110px box and draws two lines (36px tall). On P44/01-evidence/tiles/1440-00.png it breaks as 'Editor with / comment access', right-aligned, so the two lines start at different x positions.
findings.before: Role label wrapped onto two ragged right-aligned lines
findings.after: Keep the role on one line (a shorter label such as 'Can comment', or a wider role column), or let it wrap left-aligned under the name
findings.why: A two-line right-aligned label has no shared left edge and reads as two separate values.

findings.title: Prefer wrapping over truncation
findings.evidence: In dom-1440.json 'alexandra.whitfield@northwindlabs.com' is a 12px nowrap span, and the tile P44/01-evidence/tiles/1440-00.png shows it cut to 'alexandra.whitfield@northwind...'. The capture does not show whether the full address is exposed, for example in a title attribute.
findings.after: Let the chip grow to the field width, or truncate the middle of the address and keep the domain, with the full address exposed
findings.why: The truncated part is the domain, which is the piece that tells two invitees apart.

strengths: 'Bartholomew Featherstonehaugh' wraps onto two lines at 1.38 leading instead of being cut.
